questions.q: What is the complete real stack this Beginner project built, start to finish?
options: S3 raw zone -> Glue Crawler -> Glue Data Catalog table -> Athena ad hoc SQL query
S3 -> Glue ETL job -> Redshift -> Step Functions schedule
On-prem SQL Server -> Redshift -> Power BI dashboard
S3 -> Lambda function -> DynamoDB -> API Gateway
questions.explain: This project deliberately stayed at S3 + Glue Crawler + Athena — the minimal real stack for one ad hoc question.

questions.q: What were the two real complications this project handled along the way?
options: A crawler inferring a column's type slightly wrong, and a flat file layout that needed partitioning before it could scale
A failed IAM permission and a Redshift cluster outage
A missing CSV file and a corrupted S3 bucket policy
A Step Functions timeout and a Lambda cold start
questions.explain: Lesson 5 covered the order_date type-inference issue, and Lesson 8 covered retrofitting partitioning onto the flat orders-raw layout.

questions.q: What is explicitly NOT part of this project, and why not?
options: Glue ETL, Redshift, and Step Functions — because nothing in the actual requirement (one ad hoc question) called for them
S3 and Athena, because they were replaced by Redshift midway through
The Glue Data Catalog, because Athena doesn't need it
SQL queries, because this project is purely infrastructure setup
questions.explain: The lesson frames leaving these out as a deliberate act of matching infrastructure to the actual requirement, not a limitation.

questions.q: What single change in business requirement justifies the Intermediate project adding a Glue ETL job and scheduling?
options: A second stakeholder needing a repeatable, recurring dataset instead of a one-time ad hoc answer
The raw files changing from CSV to JSON format
Northfield switching from AWS to a different cloud provider
The original Operations Manager asking the exact same question a second time by coincidence
questions.explain: The shift from ad hoc to recurring is explicitly what justifies the added infrastructure — the same requirement-driven restraint this project practiced throughout.

questions.q: In the Intermediate project, how does the curated dataset's partitioning differ from how this Beginner project handled it?
options: The curated dataset is partitioned from the start, rather than retrofitted onto a flat layout after the fact like Lesson 8 did
The Intermediate project does not use partitioning at all
Partitioning in the Intermediate project is handled entirely by Redshift instead of Glue
The Beginner project's partitioning scheme is discarded and never reused
questions.explain: The lesson notes the curated dataset is built partitioned-from-the-start, contrasting with this project's after-the-fact retrofit in Lesson 8.
